text: Useful words and learning goalsUseful words: Information tells us something. A gesture is a body movement that helps send a message. An offer says what we can do for someone. A request asks someone to do something.
html:

Useful words: Information tells us something. A gesture is a body movement that helps send a message. An offer says what we can do for someone. A request asks someone to do something.

text: Useful words and learning goalsUseful words: Like means enjoy. Dislike means not enjoy. Prefer means choose one thing over another. A reason tells why.
html:
Useful words and learning goals

Useful words: Like means enjoy. Dislike means not enjoy. Prefer means choose one thing over another. A reason tells why.

text: Useful words and learning goalsUseful words: A text has a job. Recount: tell what happened. Story: tell connected events. Opinion: say what you think. Facts: information we can check.
html:
Useful words and learning goals

Useful words: A text has a job. Recount: tell what happened. Story: tell connected events. Opinion: say what you think. Facts: information we can check.

text: Useful words and learning goalsUseful words: Repeat means come back again. Rhyme means matching ending sounds, as in sun and run. Beat means steady taps. Rhythm is how we time the word sounds.
html:
Useful words and learning goals

Useful words: Repeat means come back again. Rhyme means matching ending sounds, as in sun and run. Beat means steady taps. Rhythm is how we time the word sounds.

text: Useful words and learning goalsUseful words: A title names the whole text. A heading names a section. Contents lists sections and where they start. A link can take you to another page or section.

text: Useful words and learning goalsUseful words: A sentence gives a complete idea. In a statement, a naming part tells who or what; a happening part tells what happens or what something is like.

Useful words and learning goals

text: Useful words and learning goalsUseful words: Nouns name people, places and things, including animals. Pronouns can refer to someone or something without repeating a name. Verbs tell happenings or states. Adjectives describe qualities. Adverbs can add when, where or how details.
